total_wickets.quotes: Harborstone were four down and still short of true control, which is why Owen Vale’s innings became the hinge of the match. Evan Reid gave him a quiet working partner, and for a few overs Owen seemed to be reading rather than attacking, watching which lengths stopped, which balls skidded, and where Emirates were trying to hide the field. Then the innings changed in a visible way. Owen began taking anything full through the line, anything short into the leg-side arc, and anything slightly loose with enough force to make the boundary riders retreat. Evan’s own contribution was modest, but the partnership was not modest in effect; it gave Harborstone the first stretch where they were no longer merely recovering, they were putting Emirates Bay back under pressure. Once Evan fell, Owen kept going with Luca Barrett and then Liam Frost, and the tone sharpened again. Luca’s ten was small but useful, and Liam’s unbeaten thirty mattered because he gave the late overs a second source of movement instead of leaving everything to the set batter. Owen eventually fell for a hundred that had carried Harborstone from a damaged middle position into a defendable score, and even after he went, Liam, Ryan Foster and Mason Hart kept adding enough to make the innings finish stronger than its beginning had promised. Harborstone reached 282 for eight, a total with several layers: early trouble, Isaac and Connor’s repair, Owen’s match-shaping acceleration, and the lower order’s practical late addition.
